threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still say 'the tube' instead of just 'the train' like everyone else. It's like wearing a neon sign that says 'newbie'.
Last night on the 35, a guy serenaded the whole bus with his trumpet. Didn't even get off at his stop—just played until we reached Clapham!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I heard a three-year-old negotiating with a pigeon over a crumb outside the bakery. That’s the real life here.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a currywurst stand that doubles as a late-night club—bratwurst and beats at 3 AM. It's a vibe.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can always tell by how they react to BART delays. Locals just roll their eyes and keep scrolling their phones, while newcomers look genuinely panicked.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a bus that stopped mid-route because a guy was arguing about a lost skateboard. Classic Tenderloin, where every ride’s got a twist.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think ‘poble’ means quaint village. It’s just slang here; we’re all about the hustle, not some idyllic postcard.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're new when they still think they can get breakfast before 10am. The cafés are already packed by then, especially on weekends.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the 56 bus will get you anywhere on time. Locals know to plan their life around unpredictable delays.
Heard a guy on the N37 loudly claiming he's the 'king of Brixton'—then half an hour later, he couldn’t even find his wallet.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When the kebab shop guy remembered my order, and the grandma at the corner bakery saved me her last Brezel. That's when it felt like home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find street art that not only covers walls but embraces old abandoned factories, turning them into open-air galleries.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a local brings their own bag for tacos at Taqueria La Cumbre—seriously, the takeout containers are a tragedy waiting to happen.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni with a street musician belting out 'I Will Survive' while a guy in a tuxedo tried to tap dance. Pure Tenderloin chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí. But the real vibe is in the quiet plazas where locals sip vermut and chat, far from the tourist traps.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they stand at the metro ticket machines, staring at the screen like it’s a foreign language. Classic rookie move.
